text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German bond markets were closed on Thursday for the May 1 public holiday. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.73, up 0.52 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilt futures ended election day firmer on good underlying demand as the market anticipated a Labour government taking office with a healthy majority. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-23/32, up 04/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.
FRANCE - French bonds were closed on Thursday for a market holiday.
ITALY - Italian bonds were closed on Thursday for a market holiday. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.19 up 0.57 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries climbed to session highs. Fed confirmed it was buying coupons from 11/15/07 to 02/15/27. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-17/32, up 08/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.93 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed firmer and at their session highs on Thursday, after falling nearly two yen during the three previous sessions. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.40, up 0.30 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - The May Day holiday which closed markets in many key centres on Thursday saw primary market supply dry up.

"It is going to be extremely quiet today and on Friday," a syndicate manager said. Markets are closed in among other countries Argentina, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Colombia, Ecuador, Germany, Mexico, Russia, Switzerland and Venezuela.

The British election also contributed to the lack of supply, dealers said, but added demand for sterling Eurobonds looked set to improve afterwards. Financial markets have already factored in a victory by the Labour Party, well ahead in opinion polls, and an interest rate hike of either 25 or 50 basis points, they said.
